commit_message:
cookie: overhaul and cleanup

- split the huge Curl_cookie_add() into several smaller static functions

- switch to using the common llist instead of custom linked list

- use less memory for *getlist()

- use bitfields for flags in the Cookie struct

- avoid the copy for date parsing

- more consistent variable naming

Closes #15247

fix_commit_message:
http: do the cookie list access under lock

A previous refactor of cookie logic changed Curl_cookie_getlist to no
longer return a list of copied cookies, but instead return a linked list
pointing to existing cookies. The returned linked list is accessed
outside of the scope of the cookie share lock in http_cookies, which
leads to issues if the shared cookie list is modified at the same time.
This is the relevant commit: be39ed1

Closes #18457
agent_reasoning: The cookie refactor changed Curl_cookie_getlist() to return a list of pointers into the live cookie jar instead of copied Cookie structs, but Curl_http_cookies() still released the share lock immediately after the getlist call, before iterating the list to build the Cookie header. This left a window where a second thread holding/acquiring the same share lock (e.g. processing a Set-Cookie response that frees/replaces a Cookie entry) could invalidate nodes that the first thread was still dereferencing, causing a use-after-free. The fix extends the locked region to cover the list traversal and Curl_llist_destroy() call, only unlocking once all live-pointer access is complete.
